subject: VPC performance contract: throughput expectations and egress mitigation

From: Aurelius Operations <ops@aurelius.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC performance contract: throughput expectations and egress mitigation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're starting procurement conversations internally and need a short write-up from Redwood that captures the throughput targets you can guarantee inside a VPC/private deployment, how bursting works, and what network egress controls/measurement we can expect. High-level requirements from our side:

- Baseline sustained inference: ~200 tokens/sec across our fleet (target for initial rollout).
- Peak burst: up to ~800 tokens/sec for short windows (minutes) during heavy traffic spikes.
- Deterministic tail latency: single-digit 99th percentile under baseline.
- Network egress: per-GB metering, and ability to cap egress per-project.

Can you also include operational constraints (recommended headroom, warm pools, cache-warm strategies) and a short acceptance test we can run in staging? Procurement would like anything that helps scope costs (egress + reserved capacity) and what we should expect to see in the first 30 days.

I've attached our VM matrix and a short SLA request form we use to evaluate vendors. Do you have an initial SLA draft or proposal you can share this week?

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Director, Operations
Aurelius Health
attachments: Aurelius_VM_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_request_form.pdf (pdf)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick summary up-front and then a proposed plan / test approach.

Summary (short):
- We can support a baseline tier aligned with your 200 tokens/sec ask, but we recommend sizing with ~20% compute headroom for sustained workloads to keep 99th percentile latency predictable (so plan for ~240 tokens/sec effective capacity per provisioned unit).
- Burst policy: short-term bursts up to 800 tokens/sec are supported via a warm pool + burst budget for up to 10 minutes every hour; bursts beyond that trigger automated fallback to a compatible quantized model with slightly higher latency.
- Egress controls: our Private deployment supports per-project egress metering and hard caps via the VPC control plane; billing-grade metering uses per-GB counters exported to your billing collector and Redwood Console (we can push metrics to your Prometheus if preferred).

Operational recommendations (what to provision):
- Staging: 1 dedicated GPU pod (A100x1 equiv) per dev/test cluster for acceptance testing; pre-warm KV cache with a 30-minute warmup script.
- Pilot (production baseline): start with 4 pods sized to hit ~150–240 tokens/sec each depending on model variant; this maps to the baseline SKU in our dedicated offering.
- Premium (scale target): provision autoscaling group with 8 baseline pods + 2 warm-burst pods to satisfy frequent spikes up to your 800 token/sec target.

Proposed acceptance test (staging):
1) Warmup run: replay representative prompt set (provided by Aurelius) for 20 minutes while capturing cold/hot latency and KV cache hit ratio.
2) Sustained run: 60-min sustained load at 200 tokens/sec; measure 50/95/99 pcts and token-cost.
3) Burst run: 3 x 10-min bursts to 800 tokens/sec; confirm fallbacks / failover behaviour and monitor tail latency.

Attached is a short SLA draft (redwood-private-sla-draft_v1.pdf) that outlines commitments and fallback policies. If you like this, we can convert to procurement language and produce a DocuSign-ready SOW + pricing estimate.

Notes for the team (cc'd): Laura — can you confirm the staging checklist and any additional egress guardrails we should include in the acceptance test? Ben — can you prep a ballpark cost for baseline vs premium for Aurelius and a short note on reserved capacity options (monthly vs annual)?

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding a short ops checklist and a few operational constraints to Karthik's note.

Operational checklist (staging & pilot):
- Network: verify MTU and path MTU discovery on customer VPC, ensure TCP window settings are standard (we've seen TLS handshakes add ~10–15ms on cold starts).
- Egress policing: configure per-project egress caps in the control plane and enable billing exports to S3/your collector every 15 minutes for reconciliation.
- Warm pools: keep at least one warm pod per region with KV cache preloaded during business hours (configurable).
- Scheduling windows: recommend load tests run during a pre-agreed 2-hour window; ops on-call to be present for the first two tests.
- Telemetry: enable full token-level sampling (5% sample by default) and 100% request tracing for the acceptance test.

Constraints / caveats:
- Sustained sustained ~240 tokens/sec per provisioned A100-equivalent pod assumes a 32k context and a model variant with float16 or q4_0 quantization. Smaller contexts increase throughput.
- We will require access to a representative prompt corpus for cache-warm simulations; please sanitize PHI if present.

I've attached the staging checklist (.md) that ops will use. Karthik — can we own the staging window coordination? Ben — once you have the pricing numbers, let's align on a 30-day pilot SOW (no long-term commitment) and a ramp plan to premium.

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Private Deployments Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: staging-checklist.md

Karthik / team — thanks for the detailed responses and the draft SLA. Procurement reviewed the proposal with our engineering leads and we're comfortable to move forward with a 30-day pilot. A few items before we sign anything:

- Pilot scope: Baseline pilot set to 150 tokens/sec sustained (we're conservative for the first month) with an option to move to the premium baseline (400 tokens/sec) after successful tests. Please update the SLA to reflect the pilot baseline and the ramp option.
- Cost ask: can you provide a one-page cost estimate for the pilot (baseline) and an estimated monthly run-rate for premium? Include egress per-GB pricing assumptions.
- DocuSign: we prefer a short SOW + MSA amendment. If you can push a DocuSign link we can expedite.
- Egress metering: for reconciliation, can you confirm the format of the exported CSV and whether it contains per-project tags (we require per-project tags).

Attachments: po-intent.pdf (intent to pilot). We can sign a PO once the pilot SOW and cost estimate are in hand.

Questions inline:

Please cc procurement@aurelius.com on the updated SOW.
